done_when: Forge's review brief shows the previous round's findings and asks for every blocking gap at once; a test the story assigns to another task is an advisory Later finding; the end-to-end test rule applies to user-facing behaviour, not CI, config or test-only items; the edge-case rule sits with the blocking rules; Forge's bookkeeping files are left out of the out-of-scope list; the reviewer's checkout has readable git history; tests through forge close show each

findings.body: The clone's `origin/main` tracks the source repository's local `main`, not its `origin/main` ([Git clone documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-clone)). `src/forge/close.py:170–171` fetches and merges the remote default branch into the task worktree without updating local `main`. When local `main` lags, Autoreview therefore receives an older base and reviews already-merged changes alongside this branch's changes; if the local default branch is absent, the base cannot resolve. Preserve the source base's exact commit in the clone before passing it to Autoreview. Add coverage through `forge close` with local `main` behind `origin/main`; the new history test only checks HEAD and cannot detect this mismatch.
findings.title: Preserve the fetched review base in the cloned checkout

why: Autoreview's brief from Forge makes reviews take extra rounds: findings arrive one round at a time, tests owned by a later task block, the end-to-end rule and edge cases block non-user items, Forge's own records show as out of scope, and the reviewer cannot read git history
